transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-02
Time: 15:00 PT (scheduled 60 min)
Duration: 52 minutes (recorded)
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Sarah Patel (Pinecrest - Head of ML), Tom Reed (Pinecrest - CTO), Leila Ahmad (Pinecrest - NLP Eng), Marco Silva (Pinecrest - DevOps)

Summary: High-level POC scoping for logistics document extraction / QA use case. Discussed success criteria (accuracy, hallucination tolerance), workload sizing (QPS, daily volume), benchmarks to run and timelines. Agreed to 4-week POC with bench window and a hosted vs VPC deployment evaluation.

Topics: success criteria; multilingual support (EN/ES/PT); on-prem vs VPC; model shortlist and quality/latency tradeoffs; bench plan and timeline; next steps and action owners.

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call?
[00:05] Sarah: Sarah Patel here. Hey.
[00:07] Tom: Tom Reed, CTO.
[00:08] Leila: Leila, NLP.
[00:10] Marco: Marco, DevOps.
[00:12] Diego: Diego with Redwood, SE.
[00:14] Maya: Awesome. We'll run through our typical POC scope. We're aiming for clear success criteria, a bench plan, and a proposed model shortlist.

[02:02] Maya: Can you paint the workload — rough numbers, peak patterns?
[02:10] Tom: Yeah, so daily messages that hit the NLP pipeline are about 60k per day currently, that's both inbound queries and document ingests. Peak to about 250 QPS for short windows, sustained around 40 QPS. Our initial idea is to test for a 100 QPS sustained target for the POC with bursts to 300 QPS.
[02:35] Sarah: Important to note most of these are short snippets — shipment updates, proof-of-delivery notes, and customer chat transcripts. Typical request size is 50-350 tokens, some extraction jobs are longer, up to 2k tokens for full manifest parsing.

[04:20] Diego: Ok that's helpful. For bench planning we want to cover two profiles: low-latency gen/extract for short requests, and batch long-document parsing where throughput matters. We'll propose continuous batching + prefix caching where helpful.
[04:45] Leila: Multilingual support is key — English, Spanish, and Portuguese mainly. Also domain-specific vocabulary: container IDs, incoterms, carrier codes — we can't have the model hallucinate those.

[06:00] Maya: Let's be explicit on success criteria. What are you measuring? Accuracy, p95 latency, cost, and hallucination/error rate?
[06:10] Sarah: Exactly. Our internal goal: extraction F1 > 0.92 on key fields (tracking_id, delivery_date, recipient_name), p95 latency under 350ms for short requests (<=512 tokens), and hallucination rate less than 2% on validation set. Also deterministic behavior for ID fields is non-negotiable.
[06:38] Tom: For cost, we want a ballpark that keeps per-request cost under $0.02 for typical short requests, otherwise it's not sustainable.

[08:05] Diego: Noted. On models: we'll show an open-model shortlist tuned for quantization/latency. Initial candidates: LLaMA-3 family (q4f16 variants), Mistral-instruct-ish models, and a smaller T5-like open variant for extraction-heavy paths. We should also test a larger quality model for correctness baseline — call it 'M-XL' for bench.
[08:50] Leila: A quick flag — we've seen Llama-3 do well on general QA, but it sometimes hallucinates numeric IDs. We need to test the no-hallucination constraint specifically.

[10:30] Maya: Good call. We'll add targeted hallucination tests. Diego, can you outline the bench plan?
[10:36] Diego: Sure. Week 1: infra setup and dataset ingest (we'll run hosted first for speed, then VPC). Week 2: latency and accuracy benchmarks, short-request profile and long-doc parses. Week 3: iterate on prompt engineering, quantization (q4f16, q4_0), and measure p95/p99. Week 4: final run, compare models, produce report with cost estimates and recommendations. We're thinking a total ~4 weeks.

[12:11] Marco: On infra, we need to confirm VPC peering and egress rules. We are not allowed to send PII to unmanaged endpoints for EU shipments. So any hosted test hitting EU data needs to be within EU-region or using Private deployment.
[12:35] Sarah: Right — data residency. For EU customers we must keep logs in EU and use customer-managed KMS. Can Redwood support that in POC?
[12:45] Maya: Yes — Redwood can run the POC in a Private VPC-controlled deployment or dedicated region. For the proof-of-concept we usually do a hybrid: host in Redwood EU region and then do a VPC trial if we get to dedicated. We'll share our SOC2 and KMS integration docs.

[14:10] Tom: Another constraint: Our DevOps team prefers containerized benchmark images we can run in our env. Can Redwood provide reproducible bench containers?
[14:20] Diego: Absolutely — we'll provide Docker images and a helm chart for the bench harness. That'll make it repeatable in your EKS cluster.

[16:00] Leila: About evaluation metrics: beyond F1, we want entity-level exact match for certain fields (tracking IDs), BLEU is irrelevant here. Also we want a small suite of adversarial prompts that try to induce hallucinations.
[16:20] Diego: We'll include an adversarial bench set. For the extraction path we can also evaluate a smaller deterministic model (sequence labeling) as a fallback if the generative output fails.

[18:40] Sarah: Interest in hybrid approach — gen models for fuzzy QA and an NER/seq-labeler for structured extraction. Does Redwood support routing to different model classes?
[18:52] Maya: Yes — routing policies are straightforward. You can set latency-first for short queries, or use deterministic labeler for high-confidence structured outputs. We'll demonstrate routing in the POC.

[20:30] Tom: Timeline question — if we start next week, can we deliver bench results in four weeks?
[20:36] Maya: Yes. Week 0 (this week): align on datasets and infra. Week 1: infra + ingest. Week 2: bench runs. Week 3: iterate and re-run. Week 4: final report and recommendation.

[22:15] Leila: For datasets: I'll share a 5k sample corpus with redacted PII — includes manifests, chat logs in EN/ES/PT and some noisy OCR outputs.
[22:28] Maya: Perfect. We'll need an exact label spec for the fields and a small validation set with gold labels.

[24:50] Diego: About latency targets — p95 < 350ms we can hit on optimized quantized gpus if request size <=512 tokens. For larger 2k token parses expect p95 to be >2s unless we batch it as an async job. We'll measure both synchronous and async throughput numbers.

[26:30] Sarah: For cost modeling, can Redwood provide pricing scenarios: hosted best-effort, dedicated reserved (committed), and private on-prem license? We need that to compare to our internal run-costs.
[26:45] Maya: Yes — we'll provide 3 scenarios and a unit economics spreadsheet. We'll include token-level cost, GPU-hour estimates, and ops overhead.

[29:00] Marco: Networking: Is there a requirement for outbound IPs or can we do peered VPC with private endpoints? We want no public egress for EU shipments.
[29:08] Diego: You can do VPC peering/private endpoints. We'll document the required ports and SNI certs. Also note that in VPC mode logs can be forwarded to your Kinesis/Splunk via private links.

[31:20] Leila: Model shortlist — can you enumerate recommended models and their tradeoffs?
[31:28] Diego: Sure. Shortlist: 1) LLaMA-3-medium (q4f16) — good latency and reasonable accuracy; watch for numeric hallucinations. 2) Mistral-instruct-like 7B — strong multi-lingual baseline and often better on instruction-following. 3) A distilled T5-extractor (smaller) — great for exact-field extraction, low latency. 4) M-XL (large baseline) — accuracy ceiling, used as reference. We'll include quant and float runs.

[33:10] Sarah: Can you include a Portuguese-heavy test? Our Brazil routes are sensitive to translations and cargo terms.
[33:22] Diego: Yes — we'll add a PT-heavy slice in the bench suite.

[35:00] Tom: Any concerns about model licensing? We prefer fully open-licensed models for deploy flexibility.
[35:07] Maya: All shortlisted are open models with permissive licensing; we'll call out any restriction in the report.

[36:50] Leila: On evaluation, I want to measure false positive rate on ID generation — e.g., the model inventing a tracking number when none exists. That's a critical failure mode.
[37:05] Diego: We'll add a 'hallucination detector' test and measure false positive rate per 1k requests.

[38:40] Sarah: For success sign-off, what do we need to pass?
[38:46] Maya: Passing criteria: extraction F1 >= 0.92 on the validation set, structured exact-match for ID fields >= 0.98, p95 latency <=350ms for 512-token requests in the recommended deployment, and cost per short request <= $0.02 in the preferred scenario. If we hit those, we'll recommend rollout options.

[41:15] Tom: If we miss one metric, what happens? Are we doing extension options?
[41:20] Maya: We'll include a mitigation plan — tuning, fallbacks to deterministic extractor, or recommending a dedicated capacity commitment to reduce cost.

[43:00] Marco: Security doc ask — we'll need a SOC2 summary, KMS integration steps, and how audit logs are stored.
[43:12] Maya: We'll share those by email.

[45:30] Leila: Quick note — we may want to run an internal gold-relabel step if extraction results vary too much; can we do iterative labeling during POC?
[45:40] Diego: Yes — we'll support re-scoring with updated labels and re-run the bench, that's part of the week 3 iteration.

[47:55] Maya: Ok let's capture action items.
[48:00] Sarah: Leila will send the 5k sample + labels by Friday.
[48:05] Leila: Yep, I'll send by EOD Friday.
[48:10] Maya: I'll send the bench plan and cost spreadsheet by Monday (2026-09-06).
[48:15] Diego: I'll prepare the Docker images and bench harness, aim to get them to you by 9/10.
[48:22] Marco: I'll confirm VPC peering constraints and EKS version by 9/07.

[49:00] Tom: Sounds good. Any last questions?
[49:05] Sarah: No, thanks.
[49:08] Maya: Great — we'll follow up with next steps and schedule the benchmark run. Thanks everyone.

Recap / Next Steps:
- Week 0/1: infra setup (Redwood provides images + helm), Pinecrest shares dataset and constraints.
- Week 2: run latency + accuracy benches (EN/ES/PT slices + adversarial suite).
- Week 3: iterate on prompts/quant/tuning.
- Week 4: final report with cost scenarios and recommended deployment (hosted vs VPC/dedicated).

Links/References mentioned: SOC2 whitepaper (to be shared), bench harness repo (link TBD), cost spreadsheet (attachment to come).

Transcript end.
